Consult Summary:
- 23-year-old female with several days of worsening, constant lower midline abdominal pain (8/10) and light vaginal spotting; face-to-face abdominal examination and same-day pregnancy test recommended.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Constant lower midline abdominal pain, started a few days ago, progressively worse, pain severity reported as 8/10.
- Timeline:
  - Pain began a few days prior to consultation and has been getting worse.
  - Constipation occurred last week for approximately one week; bowel habit reported as improved/normal this week.
  - Last menstrual period approximately 2–3 weeks ago.
  - Patient reports a pregnancy test was done about one month ago (result not documented).
  - Implanon contraceptive implant placed approximately one year ago.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - No specific exacerbating or relieving factors documented.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Light vaginal bleeding/spotting described as light pink/small amount separate from regular menses.
  - Occasional nausea without vomiting.
  - No fever reported; patient does not feel feverish.
  - No vomiting.
  - No urinary frequency, dysuria, hematuria, or difficulty passing urine.
  - No vaginal malodorous discharge reported (only light spotting/discharge).
  - No syncope or presyncope.
  - Able to perform normal activities and work; pain intermittently very uncomfortable.
- Review of systems / pertinent negatives:
  - No shortness of breath or shoulder pain.
  - No documented fever, no vomiting, no blood in stool or urine reported.
  - No prior pregnancies.
  - No recent significant travel within the last year (travel one year ago noted).

Past Medical History:
- Allergies:
  - Amoxicillin allergy reported.
- Medical conditions / surgeries:
  - No other medical problems reported.
  - No prior surgeries.
- Obstetric/Gynecologic history:
  - Nulligravida (no prior pregnancies).
  - On Implanon implant for contraception (inserted ~1 year ago).
  - Menstrual cycles described as irregular/sometimes sporadic while on Implanon.

Medications:
- Implanon contraceptive implant — date placed ~1 year ago (dose/route/frequency not applicable).
- No other medications documented.

Social History:
- Occupation: school teacher.
- Lives with husband and husband's family.
- Smoking/alcohol: patient responded "I don't know" when asked about smoking or alcohol (status unclear).
- Recreational drugs: denies use.
- Recent travel: traveled abroad approximately one year ago; no recent travel.

Family History:
- No family history details documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: not documented.
- Examination findings: no physical examination findings documented (patient agreed to face-to-face examination; none performed during this consult).

Investigations:
- Pregnancy test performed approximately one month ago — result not documented.
- Plan to perform a pregnancy test today (result not documented in transcript).
- No other investigations, labs, or imaging documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute worsening lower midline abdominal pain
  - Assessment: Several days of constant, progressively worsening lower abdominal pain, 8/10 severity. Associated with light vaginal spotting and nausea. Exact etiology undetermined from remote consultation.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange face-to-face clinic appointment for abdominal and pelvic examination.
    - Advise patient to contact support line to book an in-person appointment (patient agreed).
    - Urgent review recommended if symptoms significantly worsen, if unable to keep fluids down, or if new red-flag features develop.
- Issue 2: Vaginal spotting/light vaginal bleeding
  - Assessment: Light pink spotting since last period (period ~2–3 weeks ago); small amount of discharge noted.
  - Plan:
    - Perform pregnancy test today; if positive, arrange urgent in-person review.
    - Document and evaluate during planned face-to-face appointment (pelvic exam, further gynecologic assessment as indicated).
- Issue 3: Recent constipation (resolved)
  - Assessment: Constipation for ~1 week last week, now improved.
  - Plan:
    - No specific treatment documented; monitor bowel habit and address if recurrence at in-person visit.
- General plan items:
  - Pregnancy test recommended today; patient agreed to perform.
  - Face-to-face abdominal/pelvic examination arranged via support line booking.
  - Return earlier or seek urgent care if vomiting, inability to tolerate fluids, marked worsening of pain, or positive pregnancy test.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate) not documented.
  - Result of the pregnancy test performed ~1 month ago not documented.
  - Current pregnancy test result (recommended for today) not available in transcript.
  - No medication list beyond implant documented (medication reconciliation incomplete).
  - No physical examination findings or abdominal/pelvic exam documented.
  - No laboratory or imaging results provided.
  - No explicit STI or gynecologic history (e.g., prior infections, cervical screening) documented.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Timing of last sexual intercourse unclear: patient first said "four weeks ago" then corrected to "four days ago" (conflict noted).
  - Patient's answer to smoking/alcohol use was "I don't know" — unclear status.
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Portions of the audio were occasionally unclear with some fragmented responses; overall adequate to extract core clinical details but several timepoints and answers were ambiguous or imprecise.
